# trouble shooting for the diagnostics of the Cisplatin
```{r}

# check the barcod
# counts is raw matrix (genes x barcodes)
i=2

counts <- DataPipseq[[i]]      # replace i/sample
cat("Barcodes in raw matrix:", ncol(counts), "\n")
umi_per_bc <- Matrix::colSums(counts)
summary(umi_per_bc)
table(umi_per_bc > 200) 
# packages
library(Matrix)
 #BiocManager::install("DropletUtils")
library(DropletUtils)
library(Seurat)
library(SoupX)      # optional, run after emptyDrops if desired

# counts is genes x barcodes sparse matrix
# quick sanity
print(class(counts))
print(dim(counts))   # genes x barcodes

# 1) barcodeRanks to inspect and get knee
br <- barcodeRanks(counts)
summary(br$total)
# optional quick plot (interactive / save to file)
png("barcodeRanks.png", width=800, height=600)
plot(br$rank, br$total, log="xy", xlab="Rank", ylab="Total counts", main="barcodeRanks")
o <- order(br$rank)
lines(br$rank[o], br$fitted[o], col="red")
abline(v = br$knee, col="blue", lty=2)
abline(v = br$inflection, col="green", lty=2)
legend("bottomleft", legend=c("fitted","knee","inflection"), col=c("red","blue","green"), lty=1:2)
dev.off()

cat("knee:", br$knee, " inflection:", br$inflection, "\n")

# 2) Prefilter barcodes to reduce compute
# Strategy: keep barcodes with total counts >= min(100, br$knee/100) OR up to e.g. top 200k barcodes by total
totals <- Matrix::colSums(counts)
# Option A: keep barcodes with total >= 100
keep1 <- which(totals >= 100)

# Option B: if you want to keep up to top N barcodes by UMI
Ntop <- 200000
ord <- order(totals, decreasing = TRUE)
keep2 <- ord[1:min(Ntop, length(ord))]

# Combine heuristics to form final prefilter
prefilter_bcs <- sort(unique(c(keep1, keep2)))
length(prefilter_bcs)  # how many barcodes we'll run emptyDrops on

# Subset counts for emptyDrops (important to reduce memory/time)
counts_prefilt <- counts[, prefilter_bcs]

# 3) Run emptyDrops
# Lower is the minimum total count below which we don't test (set to 100 or lower for sensitive)
set.seed(100)
ed <- emptyDrops(counts_prefilt, lower = 100)
# ed is a DataFrame with p.value, FDR, etc. Many rows will be NA for extremely low totals.

# How many barcodes are called as cells?
table(ed$FDR <= 0.05, useNA = "ifany")
sum(ed$FDR <= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)  # number of barcodes with FDR <= 0.01

# 4) Get the barcodes selected as cells
called <- rownames(ed)[which(ed$FDR <= 0.05)]
length(called)  # number of called cell barcodes from this prefilter set

# Map back to original column names (if counts had colnames)
# If counts had colnames, prefilter_bcs are indices; convert indices to barcode names:
if(!is.null(colnames(counts))) {
  called_barcodes <- colnames(counts_prefilt)[rownames(ed) %in% called]
} else {
  # If no colnames, we will use indices
  called_barcodes <- colnames(counts_prefilt)[which(ed$FDR <= 0.01)]
}

# 5) Create Seurat object from called barcodes
counts_cells <- counts[, called_barcodes]  # subset original matrix by barcode names
scrna.list[[2]] <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts_cells, project =  samples[2], min.cells = 3, min.features = 100) 
# (we set min.features=0 because we already called droplets; you'll filter below)

# 6) QC: compute mitochondrial % and basic filters; adjust thresholds as needed
scrna.list[[2]][["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(scrna.list[[2]], pattern = "^mt-")  # human; change for mouse (^mt-)
summary(seu$nFeature_RNA)
# example filter: keep nFeature_RNA > 200 and pct.mt < 25
scrna.list[[2]] <- subset(scrna.list[[2]], subset = nFeature_RNA >= 200  & percent.mt < 50)
cat("Cells after QC:", ncol(scrna.list[[2]] ), "\n")

## measure the rDNA proportion for each datasets
scrna.list[[2]][["rDNA"]] <-
  PercentageFeatureSet(scrna.list[[2]], pattern = "^Rp[sl][[:digit:]]")

scrna.list[[2]][["DataSet"]] = samples[2]

### define the default with RNA
DefaultAssay(scrna.list[[2]]) <- "RNA"
# 7) Optional: SoupX ambient correction (works on raw matrices)
# If you want SoupX: provide raw (tod) and 'toc' (table of counts: cell counts) as raw and called
# Example:
# sc <- SoupChannel(tod = counts, toc = as.matrix(counts_cells))
# sc <- autoEstCont(sc)
# adjusted <- adjustCounts(sc)
```

# remove the potential doublets
```{r}

setwd(DoubletDir)
# Identify the doublet cells

FindDoublets <- function(library_id, seurat_aggregate) {
    #rnaAggr <- seurat_aggregate
  seurat_obj <- subset(seurat_aggregate, idents = library_id)
  seurat_obj <- NormalizeData(seurat_obj)
  seurat_obj <- ScaleData(seurat_obj)
  seurat_obj <- FindVariableFeatures(seurat_obj, selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)
  seurat_obj <- RunPCA(seurat_obj)
  # ElbowPlot(seurat_obj)
  seurat_obj <- FindNeighbors(seurat_obj, dims = 1:20)
  seurat_obj <- RunUMAP(seurat_obj, dims = 1:20)
  # DimPlot(seurat_obj)

  ## pK Identification (no ground-truth) ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  sweep.res.list_kidney <- paramSweep(seurat_obj, PCs = 1:20, sct = F)
  sweep.stats_kidney <- summarizeSweep(sweep.res.list_kidney, GT = FALSE)
  bcmvn_kidney <- find.pK(sweep.stats_kidney)
  pK <- bcmvn_kidney %>% 
    # select the pK that corresponds to max bcmvn to optimize doublet detection
    dplyr::filter(BCmetric == max(BCmetric)) %>%
    dplyr::select(pK) 
  pK <- as.numeric(as.character(pK[[1]]))
  seurat_doublets <- doubletFinder(seurat_obj, PCs = 1:20, pN = 0.25, pK = pK,
                               nExp = round(0.05*length(seurat_obj@active.ident)), 
                               reuse.pANN = FALSE, sct = F)
 
  # create doublet groupings and visualize results
  DF.class <- names(seurat_doublets@meta.data) %>% str_subset("DF.classifications")
  pANN <- names(seurat_doublets@meta.data) %>% str_subset("pANN")
  
  # visualize the results
  p1 <- ggplot(bcmvn_kidney, aes(x=pK, y=BCmetric)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity") + 
    ggtitle(paste0("pKmax=",pK)) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))
  p2 <- DimPlot(seurat_doublets, group.by = DF.class)
  p3 <- FeaturePlot(seurat_doublets, features = pANN)
  
  # generate the plot for the doublet distribution
 ggsave(filename = paste0(library_id,"_pKmax_distribution.pdf"), p1, height = 5, width = 6)
  ggsave(filename = paste0(library_id,"_Dimplotdoublet_distribution.pdf"), p2, height = 5, width = 5)
 ggsave(filename = paste0(library_id,"_Featureplotdoublet_distribution.pdf"), p3, height = 5, width = 5)
 
  # create a df of barcodes and doublet designations
  df_doublet_barcodes <- as.data.frame(cbind(rownames(seurat_doublets@meta.data), seurat_doublets@meta.data[[DF.class]]))
  return(df_doublet_barcodes)
}

# take an aggregated snRNA seurat object and a list of library_id to find doublets. return a df of doublet barcodes
# send DimPlot and FeaturePlot of doublets for each library to plots dir
# ensure to set up the identity as each sample

orig.ident<- levels(Idents(scrna))
#scrna.list[["0DPI"]]
# apply the findDoublets function
list.doublet.bc <- lapply(orig.ident, function(x) {FindDoublets(x, seurat_aggregate = scrna)})

list.doublet.bc %>% head()
doublet_id <- list.doublet.bc %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  dplyr::rename("doublet_id" = "V2") %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames(var = "V1") # this is the barcode column

doublet_id %>% head()
table(doublet_id) # quantify total doublet vs. singlet calls (expect ~6% doublets)
# add the meta of doublet
scrna <- AddMetaData(scrna, doublet_id)

scrna@meta.data %>% dplyr::select(DataSet, doublet_id) %>% table()

saveRDS(scrna, file = "scrna_merged_withdoublets.rds")
#scrna<- readRDS("scrna_merged_withdoublets.rds")
# remove the doublets
scrna<-subset(scrna, subset= (doublet_id == "Singlet"))
```
